title: Cut the roster from 13 to 5; collapse three maker personas into one machinist
context: Thirteen agent types is thirteen available wrong routing answers, and every description sits in the main thread's system prompt. Measured: the coordination layer of 13 Leads cost 701 agent-minutes and 24.7M tokens against the 55 workers' 547 minutes and 22.0M — the middle layer outspent the layer producing output from a quarter as many agents. Nine of the thirteen were sequential-pipeline stages, expert personas, or duplicates of skills that already existed.
options: Keep all thirteen and improve their descriptions
Delete every maker and route all implementation through fork
Cut to four read-only agents only
Cut to five: four read-only plus one maker vehicle
outcome: Five: code-reviewer, security-reviewer, conformance-auditor, researcher, machinist. Revision 1 of the SPEC deleted the maker entirely and that was wrong — isolation worktree, routing to a cheaper model, and tool restriction are available only to a cold subagent and never to a fork, which has no frontmatter and inherits main's model and tools. implementer, test-engineer and platform-engineer were three personas of one job, so they collapse into one vehicle. The name machinist was chosen because it describes how the agent works (to a finished drawing, adding no design judgment) rather than what it knows, which is the line between a legitimate role and the expert-persona anti-pattern.
